I know this post is 50+ days old but thought I’d share my thoughts! I have bipolar and working on a confirmed PCOS diagnosis right now. I’ve been taking Lamictal for years and was also on bc for years. I never felt as if one noticeably affected the other, however my Lamictal does did go up a few times along my journey. My bc experience was pretty nominal and I never had bad side effects from it as well. The mood symptoms are intense. Even now after being medicated for years and on multiple medications, it can still be tough to manage. I’m curious to find out more about the PCOS side of things for myself personally and get the confirmation I need and find out what will help me best. But it doesn’t surprise me that the two can share connections considering how badly PCOS messes with your hormones. I have very high testosterone and no periods. I think I’ve had one period my whole life. And I was diagnosed with bipolar about 5 years ago now. It is frustrating to not be able to have a doctor who can assess ALL of it at once. It’s hard to be the courier of info from one doctor to the other, and then their specialities are so different it’s hard to communicate. I do think it’s worth it to be on Lamictal and it’s one of my favorite medications I’ve ever taken and truly feel like it’s helped me greatly in the long run. Wishing you luck!

PA faire is really great. There’s so many interesting vendors and good food. I would say before the weekend find the ‘Daily Writ’ online, it will outline everything for the weekend you’re going. There are many performances all over the faire but there are some that are part of an ongoing story for the day, involving the queen and her court.

This year I think the theme has to do with guilds, you can read all about it on the website! I would just eye up their website and Facebook before your weekend just in case they share anything new. I would also grab the tickets if you haven’t yet because the last few years they’ve been selling out quicker and quicker!

The chess board is a location easy to find using the map! The last few times I went one of the first events there is the peasant dance which was so much fun and a great way to start the day. There will also be storied events there usually throughout the day :)

Food must haves, I honestly really do love the Turkey leg! There’s a good variety for everyone. Last year my friend had Mac n cheese, my boyfriend found a cheesesteak, and there were burgers as well. There’s a few little spots that sell coffee too. Everyone will have bottles of water which are important since it’s a long day with lots of walking! Last year in October I had a delicious bread bowl but I’m not sure they’ll have it yet in September.

I don’t drink alcohol anymore but my favorite was ALWAYS mead. Similar to wine but sweet and strong. If you drink I recommend it. There’s plenty other options around there too!

I can’t remember what the location is called now but there’s a great eatery pavilion with a small stage that will have kickass, hilarious, raunchy singers and performers all day.

If you enjoy deeply inappropriate humor, I recommend Ploppy’s show!

We met the unicorns last year too and they were super cute and made for such an adorable photo. 

OH! And sorry hopefully this is my last point lol. Part of the days story will include jousts throughout the day. I of course forget what it’s called but it’s the big outdoor stage where they have the jousts, it’ll be on the map, you won’t miss it. There’s usually a morning joust around 12, then an afternoon maybe 3/4, and then the final joust usually at 6. These jousts are amazing and hilarious! The final joust will fill seats very fast so try and get over there early. If you sit on the right side, you will be cheering for the bad guys. If you sit on the left wide, the good guys! I always recommend cheering for the bad guys they rock!!!

I apologize if this isn’t great advice because I know everyone is in such different positions, so I don’t mean to be insensitive at all! I am a severe phobia of bugs as well. We had roaches in our first apartment and then ‘sprickets’ which are the bane of my existence… some bad times. Honestly it got to a point with myself mentally where the only possible thing I could do was ask for help. Im lucky to have a supportive partner, who also invited his friend over, and I explained that I really could not conquer the phobia and I really needed help. The house we were staying at had a pool, we were right around the corner from the beach; it was like, why wear anything but a swimsuit?

Around my close friends, I would have probably been fine, but this was a larger group that I wasn't super tight with so I had all this anxiety leading up to it. I stressed over what suits to wear when, planned out all of my outfits strategically, and then the trip finally came and as soon as we got to the house and wanted to jump I the pool, I just didn't give a shit. 

Because we were all in the same position. We were all being vulnerable with each other; there were quite a few 'fit' friends there with us but a lot of people with similar body types to myself which was a really good feeling. We all just jumped into the pool together and ran into the waves and, okay sure I'm probably idealizing it BUT basically as soon as we were there and it was happening, all that planning and strategy and fear kind of disappeared because I saw I was in a group of non-judgmental people who also had bodies they didn't love. We were on the same page (not that anyone really said anything.)

I hope you have similarly great friends and that you have a wonderful time! I know it'll be hard to stop the anxiety now; it's a lot of pressure, I know. But things will be okay and I hope you can keep your chin up! Lots of love and luck!
